note: Which chart an artifact's EXTENSION sends it to. Added 2026-08-04 to close the router seam. The chart manifest (seed/CHARTS.json) said adding a chart takes 'a manifest row plus (if the behavior is new) three registered functions - no dispatch edit', and that was true for addressing and false for ROUTING: engine/router.py keyed Lean off a hardcoded `name.endswith('.lean')`, so no manifest row could ever route a file anywhere. This file is the missing half. Shape follows adapters/language_registry.py on claude/repo-intake-adapter, but it is wired into engine/router.py itself rather than into a parallel adapter path, because a second intake path is a second set of rules to keep in agreement. Rebased with claude/repo-intake-adapter on 2026-08-04. Two rules are adopted from that branch's registry because they are strictly better: FILENAME rules, which win over extension rules (package-lock.json is shelf, not the generic .json rule), and shelf-as-the-default for an UNKNOWN extension. The default is split in two, which neither design had: an artifact with NO extension is content-classified (a chat message id like `claude||<uuid>:3` has no name to key on and must behave as it always did), while an artifact with an extension nobody declared is SHELVED rather than read as prose.

classes.chart: enters the named chart on the strength of its extension alone, before any content rule. `chart` must name a chart declared in seed/CHARTS.json.
classes.classify: content decides - transcript, table, or prose. This is what every non-Lean artifact did before this manifest existed.
classes.reference: READ AND COUNTED, NEVER INGESTED. A held language: the engine has no chart for it, and saying so with a count is the honest form of that. Silently walking past the file is not.

rules.why: the python chart exists as of the repo-intake rebase (2026-08-04): a CHARTS.json row (tag `py`, behavior `python`) plus _nu_python, _classify_python and _segment_python. THIS ROW is the third thing that was needed and the one the old contract text never mentioned.
build recipe; no chart for it
a log file has no chart of its own, but the content rules recognise log lines and pin it as a verbatim artifact. Shelving it by extension would skip that and lose the pin.
NO extension at all. A chat message id (`claude||<uuid>:3`) has no name to key on, so content decides — exactly what the router did before any manifest existed.

the DEFAULT for an extension nobody declared, written here rather than hidden in code. Shelved, not read: an undeclared extension is more likely a binary or a generated file than prose, and reading one as prose manufactures claims from noise.
